PullRequest.Title: Install the localized policy templates with VS Code setup
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10065.

VS Code setup (User and System Installer) installs only the top-level `.admx` policy template, not the localized `.adml` files in the language subfolders (`en-us`, `de-de`, ...). Without an `.adml`, an administrator can't load the template in the Group Policy editor. The ZIP archive has every file.

This started in 1.109, when #288126 moved `policies` into its own `[Files]` entry without `recursesubdirs`. Before that, the policies were installed by the main `Source: "*"` entry, which recurses. This adds `recursesubdirs createallsubdirs` to the policies entry, matching the main entry.

### How to test
1. Build and run the User Installer.
2. Look in `<install folder>\<commit>\policies`: it has `<product>.admx` and a folder for each language with `<product>.adml`.
3. Uninstall: the `policies` folder is removed.

### Validation
Stub user installer with a `policies` folder shaped like the real build (`<product>.admx`, `en-us\<product>.adml`, `de-de\<product>.adml`), installed silently into a scratch folder:
- before: only `policies\<product>.admx` was installed (reproduces the issue);
- after: the `.admx` and both `.adml` files are installed under the versioned folder, and uninstall removes all of them;
- the System Installer compiles with the change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build the Windows user or system installer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing Gulp setup task launches one ISCC subprocess; ISCC must enumerate and read the staged policy tree and include its contents before the installer artifact is complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run ISCC to compile the installer archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess per user/system setup build, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ISCC subprocess compiled the installer but the non-recursive policies entry included only the top-level ADMX.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocess is the packaging critical path; the diff only changes which staged files it consumes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively enumerate and read policy subdirectories, then compress their ADML files into the solid installer archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 14 added ADML files in 14 fixed locale directories for current generated output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only policies/* at the top level was included, so locale subdirectories and ADML files were not read into the installer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded file reads and compression work before installer production completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The generated Windows policy tree has one ADMX plus one ADML for en-us and each of the 13 fixed entries in Languages, so the diff adds 14 bounded locale files rather than scaling with user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One existing ISCC subprocess packages the setup; the diff adds no Promise fan-out, workers, queue, or explicit concurrency and leaves processing to that single packaging invocation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used on this path. The policy files are already generated/staged before setup packaging, and every installer build reads them once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added recursesubdirs flag directly causes ISCC to traverse and package the generated locale files; generator and staging code establish the bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact generated XML byte size and compression time vary with policy count, but cardinality is fixed by 14 supported locale outputs and is small relative to the application payload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The bounded packaging I/O is necessary to deliver the required localized templates and does not establish an actionable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Download and install or update VS Code with the Windows user/system installer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Installer download transfers the setup archive; installation then extracts and writes packaged files before setup completes. The changed ADML files are on these critical paths but not on VS Code application startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer the installer archive containing the newly included compressed ADML resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One installer download with 14 additional compressible XML files; no extra network requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The downloaded installer omitted all localized ADML payloads and therefore transferred fewer compressed bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Slightly increases installer bytes on the download critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract and write localized ADML files under the versioned policies directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 14 additional file writes and locale directories per install/update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Setup wrote only the top-level ADMX from the policy tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded disk I/O before setup completion; it does not affect editor startup or rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One ADML per 14 supported locale directories, regardless of workspace, user data, extension count, or machine lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single installer invocation performs extraction/writes; the diff introduces no aggregate concurrency or independent per-user/per-item scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. A fresh installer contains the files once; each install/update writes the current version's bounded policy set.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Inno Setup recursive source inclusion necessarily packages and extracts these files, and the generator proves the fixed locale count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact transfer and disk latency depend on policy XML size and machine/network speed, but only a fixed small file set is added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The extra bounded bytes and writes are the intended product payload needed for usable Group Policy templates, with no unbounded scaling or avoidable repeated boundary work shown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Uninstall a Windows user/system installation containing localized policy templates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing uninstaller removes files tracked from the installer payload before uninstall completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete the newly installed ADML files and their locale directories through Inno Setup's tracked-file cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 14 additional file deletions and their fixed directories per uninstall.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There were no installed ADML locale files to delete.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds small bounded filesystem cleanup on uninstall only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The same fixed set of 14 localized ADML files and directories installed by this change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One uninstaller invocation; no new fan-out, parallel cleanup, or retained background resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache exists. Cleanup occurs once for the installed version and leaves no long-lived in-memory state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added installed-file cleanup implied by Inno Setup payload tracking; no evidence of orphaning or repeated cleanup exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem deletion latency varies, but the operation count is fixed and low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Cleanup cost is bounded, occurs once on uninstall, and prevents retention of the newly installed payload.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and its generator, staging, packaging, install, and cleanup paths. The change adds recursive inclusion of a fixed 14-file localized policy payload, causing small intentional archive, network, install, and uninstall I/O without hot-path execution, unbounded scaling, concurrency bursts, cache lifecycle risk, or a concrete actionable performance regression.
